status: Reviewed source integrated; main runtime dist rebuilt, focused11tests and complete6003-test integrated check pass. Native loaded-runtime acceptance pending.

trigger.failure: Synchronous kill EPERM in ChildProcess close callback escaped before original completion settled, leaving test and cleanup waiting.

implementation.completion: One promise-owned retirement attempt with captured waiter, retained original log/pipes and explicit deduped retry. Event, timer and AbortSignal callbacks retain errors instead of throwing.
implementation.stop: Uncertain until original group absence and pipe/log join; publish terminal receipt after asynchronous artifact work.
implementation.signalling: Active work uses its still-live ChildProcess closure. Post-reap retries are absence-only, never authority to signal numeric PGID. Surviving unproven groups remain uncertain.
implementation.recovery: All uncertain receipts with known PID retain absence-only owned cleanup debt, including an already-reaped leader. An initial recovery signal uses the existing recorded lstart/PGID leader identity; this is not a new kernel-birth guarantee. Unrelated operations remain available; close/closeRun cannot acknowledge surviving debt.
implementation.publication: Recheck the exact original encrypted receipt before and after absence/log hashing; deletion or replacement refuses publication. Resolved recovered effects remain interrupted, never replayed.

limitations: OS/log I/O does not carry a hard overall five-second guarantee; native shutdown has its separate original-child deadline.
No claim that arbitrary commands which escape their process group are universally reversible or terminated.
Existing starting/running recovery and historical unknown-PID uncertainty policy remain unchanged.
Source and focused tests do not establish native active/startup/private shutdown acceptance.
